method: Single printed items split from the automatic families of 1783, and of 1782 where they reach the 1783 pages (long-running ones included), every item in 3 or more papers compared by machine with every page and counted again by its opening, a sweep of word-for-word passages shared by 4 or more papers for short items the families miss, phrase searches on all 1,100 pages of 1783 in both transcriptions, reading of every hit, and scan checks of each admitted passage, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended on 23 November 2026: an item printed by more than half of the papers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4, is eligible; the items printed by every paper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news)
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1783 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 230 items found on the pages, 60 in 4 or more papers by the finder's count), and again with the families of 1782 over the 1783 pages (items_from_1782.json: 34 items, 1 in 4 or more). Every item in 3 or more papers was compared by machine with every page and counted again by its opening; a sweep of seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers found 186 runs, and the runs no finder item covers were read. Counted item by item (55 entries), 47 items meet the bar by the count of their openings (count_1783.md). The admitted and chosen items were counted again by their own words with phrase searches over all 1,100 pages in both transcriptions, and read on every page.
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended on 23 November 2026, the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; as in R-01, the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35); one affair's items as in X-1800-01; digests are not admitted; sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) as in every year. In 1783 4 to 7 papers survive for the weeks of every item in the ledger, so the bar is 4 for each; from mid-October fewer than 4 papers survive and no item can be eligible.
dispositions_summary.paper_counting: 1783 has 9 catalogue series, which are 9 papers: the Pennsylvania Packet (122 issues, to 11 October), the New-Hampshire Gazette (51), the Connecticut Courant (41, to 9 December) and the New-Jersey Gazette (29) carry most of the year; the Gazette of the State of South-Carolina survives from 16 July, the New-Jersey Journal in 4 issues to 9 April, and three Charleston papers in 6 issues of April and May. No 1783 issue has a corrected date; the release's map lists no misfiled RevX page of 1783.
